examples.en: Where do you run around like that every weekend?

examples.ko: 숙제는 안 하고 친구들이랑 밖에서 싸다니기만 해요.
examples.en: He doesn't do his homework and just roams around outside with his friends.

examples.ko: 아들이 하루 종일 싸다니다가 밤늦게 들어왔어요.
examples.en: My son wandered around all day and came home late at night.
It's raining, so where are you running around?

examples.ko: 너무 싸다니지 말고 집에서 좀 쉬세요.
examples.en: Don't go running around so much; rest at home for a bit.
My younger sibling roamed around everywhere throughout the vacation.

explain: 뚜렷한 목적 없이 여기저기 돌아다닌다는 느낌이 있고, 보통 못마땅할 때 써요. 중립적으로 '돌아다니다'라고 하면 되는 곳에 쓰면 말투가 거칠게 들릴 수 있어요. 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It suggests going here and there without a clear purpose, and it usually carries disapproval. Where neutral '돌아다니다' would do, this can sound harsh. Do not use it about someone older or senior.

examples.en: Don't hang around out until late at night; come home early.

examples.ko: 그 애는 공부는 안 하고 맨날 싸돌아다녀요.
examples.en: That kid doesn't study and is always out roaming around.
The puppy ran around the yard and got covered in dirt.
Where were you roaming around yesterday?
Please break that habit of wandering around every night.
I spent the day roaming around downtown with my friends.

explain: '싸다니다'보다 조금 더 힘주어 말하는 느낌이고, 목적 없이 계속 돌아다닌다는 못마땅함이 있어요. 사람뿐 아니라 강아지처럼 동물에게도 써요. 친한 사이나 가족 사이의 구어에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is a slightly stronger version of '싸다니다', implying aimless, disapproved-of roaming. It can also describe animals such as puppies. You often hear it in casual talk among family and friends.

examples.en: I wrapped my knee, which I hurt in a fall, with a bandage.

examples.ko: 추워서 목도리로 얼굴을 꽁꽁 싸매고 나갔어요.
examples.en: It was cold, so I went out with my face wrapped up tightly in a scarf.
His finger was cut, so I wrapped it up with a handkerchief for him.

examples.ko: 상처를 싸매기 전에 먼저 깨끗이 씻으세요.
examples.en: Wash the wound clean before you bandage it.
She wrapped the baby in a blanket and carried him.
He came to school with his leg bandaged up.

explain: 다친 곳이나 몸의 일부를 천이나 붕대로 감싸서 묶는다는 느낌이에요. '감다'보다 전체를 덮어 싼다는 느낌이 강해요. '머리를 싸매다'는 관용적으로도 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 시험 문제 때문에 모두 머리를 싸매고 고민했어요.
phrases.en: Everyone racked their brains over the exam question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 머리를 감싸는 게 아니라, 어려운 일을 해결하려고 온 힘을 다해 생각하거나 공부한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It doesn't mean wrapping your head; it means thinking or studying with all your effort to solve something hard.

explain_en: It means covering and tying up an injured spot or body part with cloth or a bandage. It feels more like wrapping the whole thing than '감다' (to wind around). '머리를 싸매다' is also a very common idiom.

examples.ko: 엄마가 우는 아이를 두 팔로 싸안았어요.
examples.en: Mom wrapped her arms around the crying child.

examples.ko: 친구는 내 어깨를 싸안고 위로해 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend put an arm around my shoulders and comforted me.

examples.ko: 추운 날 강아지를 품에 싸안아 주었어요.
examples.en: On a cold day, I held the puppy close to my chest.

examples.ko: 너무 웃겨서 모두 배를 싸안고 웃었어요.
examples.en: It was so funny that everyone clutched their stomachs laughing.
She cried for a long time, holding her child close.
I'm grateful to my senior, who embraces even my mistakes.

explain: '안다'보다 팔로 감싸듯이 안는 느낌이 강해요. 일상 대화에서는 '껴안다', '끌어안다'를 더 자주 말하지만, '배를 싸안고 웃다'나 '실수를 싸안다'처럼 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I laughed my head off watching the comedy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 배를 감싸지 않아도, 너무 우스워서 배가 아플 만큼 크게 웃는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: You don't have to actually hold your stomach; it means laughing so hard it hurts.

explain_en: It feels more like wrapping your arms around someone than plain '안다'. In daily talk people often say '껴안다' or '끌어안다' instead, but it appears in phrases like '배를 싸안고 웃다' and in the figurative sense of embracing someone's mistakes.

examples.ko: 몇 명이 실수했다고 전체를 싸잡아 비난하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't blame everyone just because a few people made mistakes.

examples.ko: 그 가게 직원들을 싸잡아서 욕하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't badmouth all the staff at that store as if they were all the same.
It's too harsh to lump us all together like that.
I feel bad because you lumped me in too.

examples.ko: 한 사람 잘못으로 팀을 싸잡으면 불공평해요.
examples.en: It's unfair to lump the whole team together over one person's fault.

examples.ko: 기자들을 다 싸잡아 나쁘게 보지는 않아요.
examples.en: I don't look down on all reporters as if they were all the same.

explain: 여러 사람이나 대상을 한꺼번에 묶어서 말할 때 써요. 보통 '싸잡아서 비난하다'처럼 부정적인 말과 함께 나와요. 따로 봐야 할 사람들을 한 덩어리로 취급한다는 불만이 담겨 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when bundling many people or things together in one statement, usually with negative words, as in '싸잡아서 비난하다'. It carries the complaint that people who should be judged separately are treated as one lump.

examples.en: I cut my long hair off with a snip at the hair salon.
Please snip the string with scissors.
Mom cut up the vegetables with quick chops.
The gardener snipped off the tree branches.
I cut my bangs off too short and I regret it.
I snipped out the paper and made a card.

explain: 가위나 칼로 단번에 베어 자르는 소리나 모양이에요. 한 번 자르면 '싹둑', 여러 번 자르면 '싹둑싹둑'이라고 해요. 같은 느낌인데 더 크고 굵은 것은 '썩둑'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound or look of cutting something in one stroke with scissors or a knife. One cut is '싹둑' and repeated cuts are '싹둑싹둑'. A bigger, thicker version of the same feel is '썩둑'.

examples.en: It's really rude to speak to an adult like that.
If you behave rudely, you'll lose your friends.

examples.ko: 저 애는 인사도 안 하고 싹수없게 굴어요.
examples.en: That kid doesn't even greet people and acts disrespectfully.
My junior was so rude that I got angry.
It feels bad to be told you're disrespectful.
My rude younger sibling has changed a lot lately.

explain: 주로 버릇없고 예의가 없는 사람이나 행동을 나쁘게 말할 때 써요. 윗사람이 아랫사람을 평하거나 뒤에서 흉볼 때 들려서, 직접 면전에서 쓰면 아주 거칠어요. 반대로 잘될 가능성이 보이면 '싹수가 있다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 저렇게 인사도 안 하면 싹수가 노랗다는 소리를 들어요.
phrases.en: If you never greet people like that, you'll be told you have no future.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘될 가능성이 전혀 안 보인다고 나쁘게 평가하는 말이에요. 주로 사람의 태도가 형편없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A harsh judgment that someone shows no sign of ever amounting to anything, usually because of a terrible attitude.
phrases.en_equiv: have no future; be a lost cause

explain_en: It is mainly used to criticize a person or behavior as ill-mannered and disrespectful. Because it is typically a senior judging a junior or gossip behind someone's back, saying it to someone's face is very harsh. The opposite is '싹수가 있다', meaning someone shows promise.

examples.en: That employee is a bit cold toward customers.
I'm sorry I answered so coldly.
His icy expression scared me at first.
She looks aloof, but she's actually very warm.
She turned away coldly and left.

examples.ko: 쌀쌀맞던 옆집 아저씨가 요즘은 먼저 인사해요.
examples.en: The neighbor who used to be so cold now greets me first.

explain: '쌀쌀하다'는 날씨에도 쓰지만 '쌀쌀맞다'는 사람의 태도나 말투에만 써요. 정이 없고 차갑게 대한다는 느낌이라 '냉정하다', '차갑다'와 비슷하지만 더 일상적인 말이에요.
explain_en: '쌀쌀하다' can describe weather, but '쌀쌀맞다' is only used for a person's attitude or tone. It means cold and unfriendly, similar to '냉정하다' or '차갑다' but more everyday.

examples.en: This idea is really neat, isn't it?
You look much fresher after the haircut.

examples.ko: 일 처리를 쌈박하게 해 줘서 고마워요.
examples.en: Thank you for handling the work so neatly.
The design was so sleek that I bought it right away.

examples.ko: 새 가게에 어울리는 쌈박한 이름이 없을까요?
examples.en: Isn't there a snappy name that suits the new shop?
I feel good because I wrapped up the presentation cleanly.

explain: 말끔하고 산뜻해서 마음에 들 때 칭찬하는 말이에요. 아이디어, 디자인, 일 처리처럼 깔끔하고 시원한 것에 써요. 글보다 말에서 편하게 쓰는 구어예요.
explain_en: It is a compliment for something clean, fresh and satisfying. It fits ideas, designs and the way a job is handled when they feel neat and crisp. It is more of a spoken word than a written one.

en: tiny savings; money in the pouch

examples.en: Grandma took out her little stash of money and gave me pocket money.
We saved up our little stash and went on a family trip.
I even spent the small savings I had set aside.
Even a little pocket money saved up feels reassuring.
My wife secretly put aside a little stash of money.

examples.ko: 형이 쌈짓돈을 털어서 선물을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: My older brother emptied his small savings and bought me a gift.

explain: 주머니나 서랍에 따로 아껴 둔 적은 돈을 말해요. '비상금'과 비슷하지만 쌈짓돈은 소소하고 정겨운 느낌이 있어요. 큰돈이 아니라 푼푼이 모아 둔 개인 돈이라는 뜻이라 '쌈짓돈을 털다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a small amount of money kept aside privately in a pocket or drawer. It is similar to '비상금' (emergency money) but has a modest, affectionate feel. It means personal money saved bit by bit rather than a large sum, and '쌈짓돈을 털다' is a common combination.

examples.en: The baby is sleeping, breathing softly.
The sound of soft, steady breathing is so cute.
My younger sibling fell asleep breathing softly beside me.

examples.ko: 아이가 쌔근쌔근 자는 모습을 한참 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the child sleeping peacefully for a long while.
The puppy also sleeps breathing softly.

examples.ko: 달리기를 하고 와서 쌔근쌔근 숨을 몰아쉬었어요.
examples.en: He came back from running and was panting for breath.

explain: 주로 아기나 어린 동물이 곤히 자면서 가늘고 고르게 숨 쉬는 모양에 써요. 달리고 난 뒤 숨이 찬 모양에도 쓰지만, 잠든 모습이 훨씬 자주 떠올라요. 따뜻하고 귀여운 느낌의 말이에요.
explain_en: It mostly describes a baby or young animal breathing thinly and evenly in deep sleep. It can also describe panting after running, but the sleeping image comes to mind first. It has a warm, cute feel.

examples.en: The baby sleeps making soft breathing sounds.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸려서 숨 쉴 때마다 쌕쌕 소리가 나요.
examples.en: I have a cold, and there's a wheezing sound every time I breathe.

examples.ko: 고양이가 쌕쌕 숨 쉬면서 자고 있어요.
examples.en: The cat is sleeping, breathing in light little breaths.
I ran here, so I'm breathing with a wheeze.
My younger sibling fell asleep snoring lightly.
I hear the child's wheezy breathing and I'm worried.

explain: 가늘고 가벼운 숨소리를 나타내요. 잠든 아기의 숨소리에도 쓰고, 감기나 숨이 찰 때 나는 쌕쌕거리는 소리에도 써요. 빠르고 힘찬 모양을 뜻하는 '쌩쌩'과 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It imitates a thin, light breathing sound. It is used for a sleeping baby's breath and also for the wheezy sound that comes with a cold or shortness of breath. Do not confuse it with '쌩쌩', which means fast and full of energy.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 넣지 않으면 음식을 썩히게 돼요.
examples.en: If you don't put food in the fridge, you'll let it rot.
What a waste, I let all the fruit go bad.

examples.ko: 재능을 썩히지 말고 한번 도전해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't let your talent go to waste; give it a try.
We let fallen leaves rot and make fertilizer.
I'm letting good clothes sit unused in the wardrobe.

examples.ko: 화분에 물을 너무 많이 주면 뿌리를 썩혀요.
examples.en: If you water a plant too much, you make its roots rot.

explain: '썩다'에 시키는 뜻이 더해져 어떤 것이 썩도록 두거나 만든다는 말이에요. 쓸모 있는 재능이나 물건을 쓰지 않고 그냥 두는 것에도 '썩히다'를 써요. 걱정을 끼친다는 뜻의 '속을 썩이다'는 '썩이다'라고 써서 '썩히다'와 달라요.
explain_en: It is the causative of '썩다' (to rot), meaning to let something rot or make it rot. It is also used for leaving a useful talent or item unused. The idiom '속을 썩이다' (to cause someone worry) uses '썩이다', not '썩히다'.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 거리를 쏘다니다가 저녁 늦게 친구를 찾아갔어요.
examples.en: After wandering the streets all day, I visited my friend late in the evening.

examples.ko: 방학인데 집에만 있지 않고 여기저기 쏘다녀요.
examples.en: It's vacation, so he doesn't stay home but roams around everywhere.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 어딜 그렇게 쏘다녔어요?
examples.en: Where did you run around like that on a rainy day?
Stop running around and do your homework at home first.
The kids are playing, running around the alley.

examples.ko: 서울을 쏘다니는 동안 길을 많이 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: While roaming around Seoul, I came to know a lot of streets.

explain: '돌아다니다'는 중립적이지만 '쏘다니다'는 이리저리 쉬지 않고 다니는 모습을 조금 못마땅하게 보는 느낌이 있어요. '싸다니다', '싸돌아다니다'와 비슷한 계열이에요. 자기 이야기를 가볍게 할 때는 괜찮지만 윗사람의 행동에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: '돌아다니다' is neutral, but '쏘다니다' carries a mildly disapproving feel about someone going back and forth without rest. It belongs to the same family as '싸다니다' and '싸돌아다니다'. It is fine when lightly talking about yourself, but don't use it for the actions of someone senior.

en: being as swift as an arrow

examples.ko: 그 사람은 신호가 바뀌자마자 쏜살같이 달려갔어요.
examples.en: As soon as the light changed, he dashed off like an arrow.
The vacation flew by in no time.
The puppy saw the ball and came running at lightning speed.
Time flies, and it's already graduation.
The bus passed by at lightning speed.
After getting the call, I rushed to the hospital as fast as I could.

explain: 형용사이지만 대부분 '쏜살같이'라는 형태로 '달려가다, 지나가다' 앞에 써요. 몸의 움직임도, 세월이 빨리 가는 것도 표현할 수 있어요. 시간에 쓸 때는 '세월이 쏜살같다'처럼 조금 문학적인 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: Although it is an adjective, it mostly appears as '쏜살같이' before verbs like '달려가다' or '지나가다'. It can describe fast movement or time passing quickly. When used for time, as in '세월이 쏜살같다', it sounds a bit literary.

examples.en: The money I earn from my side job is pretty good.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 하면 할수록 재미가 쏠쏠해요.
examples.en: The more you play this game, the more fun it turns out to be.
I sold things secondhand and the income was quite decent.
I have a hobby that gives me quite a bit of enjoyment.
If you buy during the sale, the benefits are quite good.
The part-time job income is decent, so I'm satisfied.

explain: 기대한 것보다 괜찮아서 만족스러울 때 써요. 주로 수입, 재미, 이득처럼 얻는 것이 꽤 많을 때 어울려요. 외롭다는 뜻의 '쓸쓸하다'와 발음이 비슷하지만 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used when something turns out better than expected and you are satisfied, typically for income, fun or benefits that add up to quite a lot. It sounds similar to '쓸쓸하다' (lonely) but is a completely different word.

examples.en: I can hear people whispering behind me.
Students in the classroom are whispering about something.
Please don't whisper while looking at me.
My friends were whispering about me.
What were the two of you whispering about?
We were whispering during class and the teacher caught us.

explain: 다른 사람이 못 듣게 낮은 소리로 이야기한다는 뜻인데, 보통 남의 이야기를 몰래 하는 느낌이 있어요. '쑥덕거리다'와 거의 비슷하게 써요. 공손하게 말할 때는 그냥 '속삭이다'나 '귓속말하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It means talking in a low voice so others can't hear, usually with the feel of secretly gossiping about someone. It is used almost the same as '쑥덕거리다'. For a neutral or polite tone, people just say '속삭이다' or '귓속말하다'.

examples.en: After the typhoon passed, the village was left in ruins.
The room where the kids played is a total mess.
The fields were turned into wasteland by the flood.
Wherever my younger sibling has passed is always a wreck.
It took a whole day to clean up the wreckage.

examples.ko: 싸움 때문에 가게가 쑥대밭이 될 뻔했어요.
examples.en: The shop nearly got wrecked because of the fight.

explain: 뜻 그대로의 쑥밭보다는 '쑥대밭이 되다, 쑥대밭으로 만들다' 형태로 엉망이 되어 망가진 곳을 가리킬 때 많이 써요. 재난 뉴스의 심각한 상황에도 쓰고, 어질러진 방을 과장해서 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: Rather than its literal meaning of a field of mugwort, it is mostly used in the forms '쑥대밭이 되다' and '쑥대밭으로 만들다' for a place left in ruins. It appears in serious disaster news and also as an exaggeration for a messy room.

examples.en: The villagers whispered to each other after hearing the rumor.
You shouldn't whisper during a meeting.
The two whispered something and then suddenly laughed.
I heard whispering in the hallway.

examples.ko: 내 앞에서 쑥덕거리지 말고 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't whisper in front of me; just tell me.

examples.ko: 이웃들이 새로 이사 온 집을 두고 쑥덕거려요.
examples.en: The neighbors are whispering about the family that just moved in.

explain: 소문이나 남의 흉을 몰래 주고받는 장면에 써서 부정적인 느낌이 강해요. 그냥 조용히 말하는 것은 '속삭이다'라고 해요. '쑤군거리다'와 바꿔 써도 돼요.
explain_en: It is used for secretly trading rumors or gossip about others, so it feels negative. Simply speaking quietly is '속삭이다'. You can swap it with '쑤군거리다'.
